17 	[Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) changes what a `<Link>` downloads for a Cache Components route. With Partial Prefetching enabled, a `<Link>` prefetches the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell): its static content and the cached content that doesn't depend on the URL. Next.js builds one App Shell per route and reuses it for every link to that route, rather than prefetching each link separately as it did before.

19 	To prefetch more than the App Shell, a link can opt into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch can then resolve cached URL-specific content that depends on `params`, `searchParams`, or the full URL.

21 	Along the way, Next.js surfaces [instant navigation](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) insights in development, naming the link or route to change.

Done. The build passes with both Cache Components and Partial Prefetching enabled. Here's what changed and why:

## Changes

next.config.ts — enabled partialPrefetching: true. This is required for the prefetch() function to take effect (it needs cacheComponents, which was already on). With it on, a default <Link> into /product prefetches only the route's App Shell — its static content plus cached content that doesn't depend on the URL.

app/product/page.tsx — extracted the related-products list into an async <RelatedProducts /> component wrapped in <Suspense>, with await prefetch() placed above the data fetch. Per the [prefetch() docs](node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/04-functions/prefetch.md), everything below that call is kept out of the App Shell, so it is not included in the default <Link> prefetch. The Suspense fallback (Loading related products…) ships in the shell; the actual list does not. The content below prefetch() resolves on a per-link prefetch or on the navigation itself.

app/page.tsx — set prefetch={true} on the featured-product <Link>. With Partial Prefetching, prefetch={true} opts into per-link prefetching, which resolves the content deferred by prefetch(). So when a user navigates from this specific link, the related products are already fetched and ready immediately.

## How the two requirements are met

- Related products out of the default prefetch: A plain <Link href="/product"> (the auto/null default) prefetches only the App Shell. Since getRelatedProducts() sits below await prefetch(), it's excluded from that shell — the default prefetch downloads only the heading, description, and the loading fallback, not the related list.
- Ready immediately from the featured-product link: That link uses prefetch={true}, which triggers a per-link prefetch that resolves the deferred prefetch() content. By the time the user clicks through, the related products are already in the client cache, so navigation is instant.

One note: getRelatedProducts() uses 'use cache' with cacheLife('hours'), which satisfies the ≥5-minute stale requirement for content to be eligible for per-link prefetch resolution (rather than streaming in only on navigation), so the related list will actually be carried by the prefetch={true} request and not just deferred to click time.
